subject: Data transfer scopes and no-model-learning playbook
messages:
From: Lauren Peterson <lauren.peterson@curatechhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@curatechhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data handling for pilot — training & transfer clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're lining up a short pilot (500k interactions) and procurement/legal asked for a few clarifications to include in our DPA amendment before we kick off:

- Explicit no-model-learning commitment: we need Redwood to confirm that customer data for this pilot will not be used to train or fine-tune models (including downstream derivatives) unless we opt in in writing.
- Prompt/response ownership: confirm that our prompts and generated responses remain our data and that Redwood will not assert any IP of derivatives produced from our inputs.
- Subprocessors & transfers: we need the current subprocessor list and a mechanism to gate any subprocessor that would be used for training/analytics. Also clarify cross-border transfer lanes (we prefer US-only processing for this pilot).
- Evidence & audit: procurement has requested an evidence pack (audit logs, subprocessor attestations, KMS routing) that will be reviewed by our security team.

Attached are our legal redlines to the DPA — high level asks are above. Can you confirm what we can get as a matter of product/config (no-learn toggle, session retention, KMS options) and an approximate timeline to deliver the evidence pack?

Goal: sign DPA amendment and start pilot the week of Apr 12th.

Appreciate it —
Lauren Peterson
Senior Counsel, CuraTech Health
lauren.peterson@curatechhealth.com
procurement@curatechhealth.com

Attachment: curatech-legal-redlines.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Peterson <lauren.peterson@curatechhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@curatechhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data handling for pilot — training & transfer clarifications

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Quick summary up front and then next steps: we can meet your core asks for the pilot with a combination of config options and a DPA amendment. High-level answers: 

1) No-model-learning: we offer an enterprise "no-model-learning" configuration that prevents ingestion into any model-improvement pipelines. Practically that's an operational and config-level toggle that (a) prevents retention in training stores, (b) disables downstream ML pipelines from consuming pilot data, and (c) marks telemetry as "non-improvable." We will provide contract language to lock that behavior for the pilot period.

2) Prompt/response ownership: Redwood will not claim ownership of customer prompts/responses. We can add explicit language that derivatives produced from your inputs are licensed to you for your use and that Redwood will not assert derivative IP over pilot outputs.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: current subprocessor roster is attached (CSV). For the pilot we can gate any subprocessor that would materially process data for training; we can commit to US-only processing for this pilot and route to onshore KMS or customer-managed keys where required.

4) Evidence & audit: we can produce an evidence pack including audit logs, subprocessor attestations, KMS routing proof, and a short runbook showing how the no-learn setting is enforced. Turning this around will take ~7 business days from approval.

Next steps I propose:
- We circulate a short DPA amendment (I attached a working draft).
- Internal check (cc'ing Kimberly & David) to confirm the operational controls and timing.
- Quick call with security (Lauren + their security engineer) to walk the evidence pack and handoff timeline.

I'll follow up internally and come back with the operational timeline and a redline you can use. If helpful, we can lock the pilot's no-learning toggle in our tenant config the day we sign the amendment so the only remaining work is evidence delivery.

Cheers,
Olga
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-no-learn-sprint.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.peterson@curatechhealth.com, procurement@curatechhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Data handling for pilot — training & transfer clarifications

Team — forwarding Lauren's asks from CuraTech. Key asks we need to confirm quickly:

- Can infra guarantee US-only processing for pilot IDs and provide a routing proof? They want an onshore-only lane (no EU/APAC transfers).
- Can we produce an evidence pack (audit logs showing data flow, subprocessor attestations, KMS routing, and a short runbook) within ~7 business days after amendment signoff?
- Product feasibility: confirm implementation steps for the "no-model-learning" tenant toggle: retention pruning, blocking model-improvement consumers, and ensuring prompt/response custody mapping so customers can assert IP for outputs.
- Legal: Kimberly, can you propose DPA amendment language that covers (1) absolute no-learning for the pilot period (unless customer opts in in writing), (2) explicit assignment/licensing language for outputs, and (3) subprocessor gating + notification?

I've attached a draft amendment and the subprocessor roster we currently publish. If we can get short answers by EOD we'll route a DPA redline back to CuraTech and lock the tenant config.

Thanks —
Olga

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.peterson@curatechhealth.com, procurement@curatechhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data handling for pilot — training & transfer clarifications

Hi all — quick operational confirmation from infra/ops:

- US-only processing: feasible. We can pin the pilot tenant to US regions and ensure no replication to other regions for the pilot data feed. We'll provide a signed attestation and a routing snapshot from our orchestration layer showing which endpoints/processes touched pilot data.

- No-model-learning toggle: product already supports a tenant-level flag that prevents messages from being copied to training stores and prevents downstream consumers (feature store, feature-extract jobs) from accessing KV/prompt streams. Implementation checklist:
  * Toggle flips retention policy to session-only (48 hours default for pilot, adjustable).
  * KV/prefix caching remains available with explicit TTL; we tag pilot data with a "no_learn" metadata key so telemetry pipelines skip it.
  * We will instrument an immutable audit trail entry when toggle is set/changed and include that in the evidence pack.

- KMS / key routing: we can offer two options — Redwood-managed US KMS with onshore keys or customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) in an onshore HSM. Both options will be documented and we will include key rotation/audit logs in the pack.

- Evidence pack ETA: given approvals we can assemble logs, attestations, and the runbook within 6 business days. Deliverables will include: routing snapshot, subprocessor attestations, audit log extracts (redacted per privacy), toggle-change audit, and a short operations playbook describing how the no-learn enforcement works.

I'll prepare the routing snapshot and a one-page operations summary for legal review. Kimberly, for the DPA wording I suggest we reference the toggle and operational controls rather than sweeping absolute language — that makes the assurance verifiable in the evidence pack. Happy to sync if you prefer a phone call.

-David
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
